title: Helper invocation execution and memory side-effect policy on shared CUs

normative_context.title: GLSL ES3.20 helper-invocation side-effect rules
normative_context.scope: The hardware plan requires helper execution separated from side effects; later GLSL ES also describes suppressed buffer/image stores and atomics. This is not an API-version/conformance claim. Bounded internal private storage and scalar uniform instruction treatment are implementation contracts.

contract.launch: Trusted KernelInvocationPolicy carries a workgroup helper bitmap plus private base/byte bound. Job/workgroup dispatch snapshots it, slices by logical warp, masks tail bits and attaches policy to physical warp initialization. GpuCore retains one per-warp record. Existing host MMIO and shader ISA/preloads/kernarg offsets remain unchanged.
contract.execution: Helpers remain in the architectural execution mask for arithmetic, loads and existing quad exchange. Memory instructions retain the admitted policy through held requests/completions. No coverage-mask substitution for shader execution.
contract.vector_stores: After effective addresses form, suppress helper store lanes unless the whole element fits trusted private bounds. This precedes local/global routing, coalescing and translation. All-suppressed stores complete without a downstream request. Fault masks include only lanes actually sent to memory. Strided/indexed and byte/half/word cases use the same rule.
contract.scalar_and_fp_stores: An instruction with an active real invocation retains existing uniform scalar/FP store behavior. Helper-only paths suppress external stores before alignment/translation, while permitting whole accesses to internal private scratch/payload storage. Loads retain helper participation and existing faults.
contract.atomics: Helper-only scalar AMOs on both local and global routes issue no request and retire with internal zero oldValue; active real invocations keep existing behavior. No helper private-memory exception for atomics. General per-invocation/vector atomic-resource support remains separate.
contract.private_range: Trusted owner metadata must describe validated non-aliasing private scratch/payload storage, not an externally visible buffer/image/framebuffer binding. Empty/overflowed ranges and ranges overlapping the shared-memory window grant no helper-store exception. Per-invocation language-private addressing is a compiler/owner contract, not arbitrary graphics-resource binding.
contract.native_workers: KernelFragStage derives masks from covered records at launch, snapshots the nine-array kernarg prefix and preserves masks across double-buffered batches. Serial RenderPipeline and parallel workers supply policy to KernelShaderStage; shared/private CU adapters carry it. Native local payload and memory-backed modes retain prefix offsets and lease ownership.
contract.compute_boundary: GpuCommandProcessor, host MMIO producer and compute-only/mixed CU dispatch paths clear graphics invocation metadata for host compute. Shared graphics packets preserve trusted policy with existing tags and credits.
contract.limits: Static raster helper policy, not dynamic discard/demotion, shader-visible gl_HelperInvocation delivery, general resource-table/alias validation or full divergent/fault/API qualification.

validation.native_source_note: Native validation began before the final archive. The only intervening source edit expanded HelperInvocationPolicySpec vector tests, which are covered by the42-check frozen run; native-tested hardware and native test sources were unchanged.
coverage: Two14-case scalar/FP tests: private boundaries, suppressed external misalignment, real/helper active-path masks, helper loads, invalid private bounds, captured policy and held replies.
Twelve vector cases: mixed private/external lanes, zero-request suppression, helper loads, original execution masks, filtered faults, indexed/strided addressing and byte/halfword boundaries.
Thirty-seven scalar AMO cases across all9operations, local/global paths, private atomic suppression and helper misalignment suppression.
4lane/3warp tail slicing and16lane/8warp128-bit helper transport with held offers and source mutation.

Real4lane/2warp CUs, local and memory-backed modes,4kernels each: mixed/all/whole-warp/no helpers, helper private outputs and quad exchange, exact external vector/scalar/FP stores, atomic suppression, reuse and held completion.
Overlapped fragment batches with masks2a/a5,288-byte private prefixes, bank snapshots, held launch and9covered retirements.
Core/dispatch/memory regressions cover compute with zero policy, initialized warp contexts, scalar/FP/vector execution and existing memory/atomic behavior.
Host command queues clear poisoned policy; shared CU routing preserves graphics policy while sanitizing compute across1/2/4CUs.
Native shared-CU payload reservation/export/release/cancellation/fault/reuse checks plus consecutive quad slot reuse and helper derivative execution.
validation.limits: Representative internal-policy qualification. General FP32 fragment payload delivery, dynamic helper/discard state, shader-visible helper built-ins, resource binding, alias ownership and API conformance remain open.

emission.scope: Default16lane/8warp CU and Mobile programmable renderer. Eight physical warp records; four parallel fragment workers and no embedded renderer CU or payload pool. The CU uses the existing arithmetic and SRAM hierarchy; policy adds register snapshots/control/checks, no SRAM array or arithmetic lane. Other queue/dispatch snapshots are additional. No synthesis PPA result.

remaining: General FP32 fragment-input staging/shader delivery and native geometry/bin/fragment ownership.
Dynamic discard/demotion, helper built-ins, full divergence/fault semantics, typed image/buffer resources and physical allocation/alias validation.
Point/line/guard-band rasterization, qualifiers, complete outputs/built-ins, numeric/invariance, transform feedback/query/watchdog behavior.
Production storage/timing/power/throughput budgets, synthesis and remaining H0-H8 gates. PPA screening is synthesis only; no place-and-route.
